# .github agent notes

- Gate publishes through the default-branch `.github/workflows/release-publish.yml` reusable workflow; the default-branch-only release-please workflow calls it with the selected tag as input, including after its repository-dispatch rerun, so tag-authored workflow steps never receive write credentials. Its release and container paths have two trust zones: `release-build`/`image-build` run the checked-out tag with `contents: read` and stage allowlisted release assets/OCI archives, while fresh `publish-release`/`publish-images` jobs check out nothing and alone hold `contents: write`/`packages: write`. Keep workflow-level permissions empty, checkout credentials disabled in code-running jobs, and the artifact handoffs explicit; contracts live in `ci_write_token_isolation_test.go`. The final release guard re-reads GitHub rather than trusting local output (`release_asset_verification_test.go`) and must remain the publisher's last step.
- Releases already published with no assets are repaired by `.github/workflows/release-repair.yml` (manual dispatch from the default branch, contract pinned by `release_repair_workflow_test.go`). Its two-job boundary is load-bearing: only `build` checks out and runs the selected tag with `contents: read`, while fresh `publish` has `contents: write`, checks out nothing, and uploads only the allowlisted artifact; the workflow has no ambient permission and no registry scope, so a backward `ghcr.io/minekube/gate:latest` retag is unrepresentable. The repair procedure and historical-tag gotchas are in `.agents/skills/release-repair/SKILL.md`.
- golangci-lint intermittently never loads the package graph on GitHub's runners (`can't run linter goanalysis_metalinter` / `could not load export data: no export data for …`, exit 3, or a burst of bogus `(typecheck)` diagnostics on a tree that compiles) and reports no finding at all. Both lint jobs therefore run `.github/scripts/run-golangci-lint.sh`, never a bare `golangci-lint run`: it warms the build cache (`go build ./...`, which also makes a real compile error fail as one), cleans the linter cache, retries ONLY that loader class (loader signature, exit 3, or a typecheck-only report), and propagates the linter's own exit code — findings are never retried. The wrapper carries its own `--self-test` (stubbed go/golangci-lint, no network) which both workflows run before linting; contract in `lint_and_release_flake_test.go`. This is release-critical: `trigger-release / lint` gates every publish job, so a flake there is a silent no-release (v0.79.1 shipped 0 assets until a re-dispatch).
- Release Please serialises its runs (`concurrency: release-please-<repo>`, `cancel-in-progress: false`) because two runs dispatched in the same second on 2026-11-13 both created a GitHub release for v0.79.1 — one with the 12 assets, one with none — and `/releases` and `/releases/latest` order by id, so the empty object became "the newest release". The publisher's final guard re-reads the release and additionally fails when a tag carries more than one release object (`lint_and_release_flake_test.go`); assets are uploaded before that check, so a duplicate is a delete-the-surplus-object task, not a re-publish.
- `trigger-release / publish-images` copies the staged OCI layouts with `oras cp --from-oci-layout`, and **oras re-reads each manifest it just pushed from the destination** (oras 1.3.0 `cmd/oras/internal/display/status`: `TextCopyHandler.PostCopy` → `graph.FilteredSuccessors(dst)`) to print its successors' status lines. A registry that has not yet made an accepted manifest readable therefore aborts the copy with `Error response from registry: sha256:<digest just pushed>: not found` — measured on v0.79.0 (job 131960268990) and v0.80.1 (job 131992784822), which published the GitHub release assets, pushed the child manifests, never pushed the top-level index, and so left **no image at all** in `minekube/gate` and `minekube/gate/jre` while `dispatch-moxy-bump` was skipped. The step now attempts both images and retries ONLY that registry read-after-write class (bounded, the copy is idempotent — every node that landed is `Exists` next attempt), and the following `Verify published container images` step fails closed unless `${IMAGE_TAG}`, `latest` and the release tag all resolve to the staged digest with both platform manifests readable; contracts in `publish_images_readback_test.go`. Do not "fix" this by retrying everything (a source-side miss carries the media type: `sha256:…: application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+gzip: not found` and must fail immediately) or by removing the read-back.
